result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 3 FOUND, 2 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full existing application assessment, including unchanged source, scoped exclusively to eShopModernizedNTier. Reviewed 27 first-party source/config/project files plus Docker Compose configuration; source-to-sink inspection and whole-scope pattern searches, not a diff review.

Limitations: static source analysis only; application not executed, no exploit or load tests, runtime deployment/ACLs and platform internals not inspected. Generated code, obj/bin, .vs, temp and vendor artifacts excluded from CWE checklist source review. NOT_FOUND means no confirmed pattern in reviewed first-party code, not proof of absence. Specialist returned change-only results and was not used as full-workspace evidence.

All first-party configuration and source scanned for secrets, cryptographic key material, authentication/authorization, permissions and logging. Secret literals are deliberately redacted in evidence. No hard-coded cryptographic key found. Runtime filesystem/SQL permissions and IIS authentication inheritance are unknown; network exposure or requirePermission=false on a configuration section alone is not proof of CWE-732, so it remains NOT_FOUND. Deployed infrastructure may provide independent audit logs.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: Confidence: high that reusable credentials are hard-coded; deployment use not verified. Docker Compose supplies a literal SQL administrator password through SA_PASSWORD, embeds the same authentication secret in the application ConnectionString, and provides a literal password argument to the sqlcmd healthcheck. All password values are [REDACTED]. CatalogConfiguration.ConnectionString (src\\eShopWCFService\\Models\\Infrastructure\\CatalogConfiguration.cs:16-17) reads the environment and EntityModel consumes it. Anyone with access to the tracked configuration obtains the configured database credential if deployed unchanged; host port mapping also exposes SQL subject to host firewall/network policy. This is repository configuration evidence, not proof the credential is currently active.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: Confidence: high for absence of application-level mutation audit events; medium for deployed audit coverage. CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, RemoveCatalogItem and CreateAvailableStock mutate catalog/inventory state and call SaveChanges without recording actor, operation, target or outcome. Full first-party source/config search found no audit logger or event source. Remote catalog/inventory changes therefore have no application-supplied security audit trail. IIS request logs, SQL audit or other deployment-level monitoring might exist outside this repository and were not inspected; this finding does not assert their absence.
